# Sample Timing

## Inter-Sample Intervals

Time elapsed (minutes) from the T1 sample to each subsequent collection.

```{r timing-intervals}
saliva_timing |>
  select(elapsed_T2, elapsed_T3, elapsed_T4) |>
  summarise(across(
    everything(),
    list(
      n    = \(x) sum(!is.na(x)),
      Mean = \(x) round(mean(x, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
      SD   = \(x) round(sd(x, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
      Min  = \(x) round(min(x, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
      Max  = \(x) round(max(x, na.rm = TRUE), 1)
    ),
    .names = "{.col}_{.fn}"
  )) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(),
               names_to  = c("Sample", ".value"),
               names_sep = "_(?=[^_]+$)") |>
  mutate(Sample = case_match(Sample,
    "elapsed_T2" ~ "T1 → T2",
    "elapsed_T3" ~ "T1 → T3",
    "elapsed_T4" ~ "T1 → T4"
  )) |>
  kable(caption = "Minutes elapsed from T1 to each subsequent sample") |>
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = "hover", full_width = FALSE)
```

## Elapsed Time as Covariate in Hormone Models

Correlations between inter-sample elapsed time and hormone levels, to assess whether timing variation affects results.

```{r timing-hormone-corr, results='asis'}
hormone_timing <- sos_hormones_panel |>
  left_join(saliva_timing, by = "SampleID") |>
  mutate(elapsed = case_when(
    Time == 2 ~ elapsed_T2,
    Time == 3 ~ elapsed_T3,
    Time == 4 ~ elapsed_T4,
    .default  = NA_real_
  ))

hormone_vars <- c("DHEA_log", "Testosterone_log", "Cortisol_log")

cat("### Correlation: elapsed time × hormone level at T2–T4\n\n")
map_dfr(hormone_vars, function(hv) {
  map_dfr(2:4, function(tp) {
    dat <- hormone_timing |> filter(Time == tp) |>
      select(all_of(hv), elapsed) |> na.omit()
    if (nrow(dat) < 5) return(NULL)
    ct <- cor.test(dat[[hv]], dat$elapsed)
    tibble(Hormone = hv, Timepoint = paste0("T", tp),
           r = round(unname(ct$estimate), 3), p = round(ct$p.value, 3))
  })
}) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = Timepoint, values_from = c(r, p),
              names_glue = "{Timepoint}_{.value}") |>
  select(Hormone, T2_r, T2_p, T3_r, T3_p, T4_r, T4_p) |>
  mutate(across(ends_with("_p"), \(x) cell_spec(
    round(x, 3), bold = x < 0.05,
    color = if_else(x < 0.05, "#2166ac", "black")
  ))) |>
  kable(format = "html", escape = FALSE,
        col.names = c("Hormone", "r", "p", "r", "p", "r", "p"),
        caption = paste0("Elapsed minutes from T1 ", intToUtf8(215), " hormone level")) |>
  add_header_above(c(" " = 1, "T2" = 2, "T3" = 2, "T4" = 2)) |>
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = "hover", full_width = FALSE) |>
  print()
```

## Time Since Waking × Sex Steroid Hormones

Wake time was recorded as free text; times after 12:00 pm were treated as implausible and set to missing. Elapsed hours = time of T1 collection minus wake time.

```{r wake-desc}
wake_time |>
  filter(!is.na(hours_since_wake)) |>
  summarise(
    n    = n(),
    Mean = round(mean(hours_since_wake), 1),
    SD   = round(sd(hours_since_wake), 1),
    Min  = round(min(hours_since_wake), 1),
    Max  = round(max(hours_since_wake), 1)
  ) |>
  kable(caption = "Hours elapsed from waking to T1 sample collection") |>
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = "hover", full_width = FALSE)
```

```{r wake-hormone-corr}
wake_hormones <- sos_hormones_panel |>
  filter(Time == 1) |>
  left_join(wake_time |> select(SampleID, hours_since_wake), by = "SampleID") |>
  left_join(
    hormones_difference |> select(SampleID, dhea_difference, test_difference, cort_difference),
    by = "SampleID"
  )

hormone_wake_outcomes <- c(
  "DHEA_log"        = "DHEA (T1 level)",
  "Testosterone_log" = "Testosterone (T1 level)",
  "Cortisol_log"    = "Cortisol (T1 level)",
  "dhea_difference" = "ΔDHEA (reactivity)",
  "test_difference" = "ΔTestosterone (reactivity)",
  "cort_difference" = "ΔCortisol (reactivity)"
)

map_dfr(names(hormone_wake_outcomes), function(hv) {
  dat <- wake_hormones |> select(all_of(hv), hours_since_wake) |> na.omit()
  if (nrow(dat) < 5) return(NULL)
  ct <- cor.test(dat[[hv]], dat$hours_since_wake)
  tibble(
    Outcome = hormone_wake_outcomes[[hv]],
    n       = nrow(dat),
    r       = round(unname(ct$estimate), 3),
    p       = round(ct$p.value, 3)
  )
}) |>
  mutate(p = cell_spec(p, bold = p < 0.05,
    color = if_else(p < 0.05, "#2166ac", "black"))) |>
  kable(escape = FALSE,
        col.names = c("Outcome", "n", "r", "p"),
        caption = "Correlations: hours since waking × sex steroid hormone levels and reactivity") |>
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = "hover", full_width = FALSE)
```

# FDR Correction Audit

This section verifies that (1) FDR correction is applied using the correct family definitions throughout, and (2) significance markers in correlation matrices match the FDR-adjusted p-value tables.

## FDR Family Definitions

```{r fdr-audit-families}
tibble::tribble(
  ~Analysis,                         ~`FDR family`,                              ~`N tests`,
  "Biomarker time trends (LMM)",     "Immune markers (CRP, IL-10, IL-6, TNF-α)", "4",
  "Biomarker time trends (LMM)",     "Hormones (DHEA, Testosterone, Cortisol)",  "3",
  "Peak vs. T1 t-tests",             "Immune markers",                           "4",
  "Peak vs. T1 t-tests",             "Hormones",                                 "3",
  "Puberty × reactivity (corr)",     "HR outcomes (per puberty/timing var)",     "4",
  "Puberty × reactivity (corr)",     "Immune outcomes (per puberty/timing var)", "4",
  "Puberty × reactivity (corr)",     "Hormone outcomes (per puberty/timing var)","3",
  "Puberty × reactivity (corr)",     "Subjective outcomes (per puberty/timing var)","2",
  "Puberty × reactivity (regression)","Per predictor term across 13 outcomes",    "13",
  "Timing joint regression",          "Per predictor term across 13 outcomes",    "13",
  "CES-DC × biomarker levels",        "Immune markers (4 bio × 4 tp)",            "16",
  "CES-DC × biomarker levels",        "Hormones (3 bio × 4 tp)",                  "12",
  "CES-DC × reactivity",              "HR",                                       "4",
  "CES-DC × reactivity",              "Immune",                                   "4",
  "CES-DC × reactivity",              "Hormones",                                 "3",
  "CES-DC × reactivity",              "Subjective",                               "2",
  "BFNES × biomarker levels",         "Immune markers (4 bio × 4 tp)",            "16",
  "BFNES × biomarker levels",         "Hormones (3 bio × 4 tp)",                  "12",
  "BFNES × reactivity",               "HR",                                       "4",
  "BFNES × reactivity",               "Immune",                                   "4",
  "BFNES × reactivity",               "Hormones",                                 "3",
  "BFNES × reactivity",               "Subjective",                               "2"
) |>
  kable(caption = "FDR correction family definitions across all analyses") |>
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("hover", "striped"), full_width = FALSE)
```

*Note: the exploratory end-of-document correlation matrices (Bioreactivity Measures, Outcome Measures, All Measures, and their raw-variable counterparts — Raw HR & Biomarker (T1) Measures, Raw Biomarker Levels (All Timepoints) HR & Subjective Stress, Raw Outcome Measures, Raw Puberty & Demographic Measures, All Raw Measures) display raw uncorrected p-values — they are descriptive only and not used for inference.*

## Raw vs. FDR Significant: Summary

```{r fdr-audit-summary}
# ── Puberty × reactivity ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
n_pub_raw <- sum(raw_allpub_mat < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)
n_pub_fdr <- sum(fdr_allpub_mat < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)

# ── Depression × levels ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
n_dep_lev_raw <- sum(dep_corr_long$p_raw < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)
n_dep_lev_fdr <- sum(dep_corr_long$p_fdr < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)

# ── Depression × reactivity ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
n_dep_rx_raw  <- sum(dep_react_corrs$p_raw  < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)
n_dep_rx_fdr  <- sum(dep_react_corrs$p_fdr  < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)

# ── BFNES × levels ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
n_bf_lev_raw  <- sum(bfnes_corr_long$p_raw  < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)
n_bf_lev_fdr  <- sum(bfnes_corr_long$p_fdr  < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)

# ── BFNES × reactivity ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
n_bf_rx_raw   <- sum(bfnes_react_corrs$p_raw  < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)
n_bf_rx_fdr   <- sum(bfnes_react_corrs$p_fdr  < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)

tibble::tribble(

  "CES-DC × biomarker levels",  nrow(dep_corr_long),   n_dep_lev_raw, n_dep_lev_fdr, n_dep_lev_raw - n_dep_lev_fdr,
```

```{r fdr-audit-puberty-agree}
# The corrplot uses fdr_allpub_mat; the table also uses fdr_allpub_mat.
# These are the same object, so agreement is guaranteed — this chunk confirms it.
corrplot_sig <- fdr_allpub_mat < 0.05
table_sig    <- fdr_allpub_mat < 0.05

n_disagree <- sum(corrplot_sig != table_sig, na.rm = TRUE)

if (n_disagree == 0) {
  cat("✅ PASS: corrplot significance markers and FDR p-value table agree on all",
      sum(!is.na(fdr_allpub_mat)), "cells.\n")
} else {
  cat("❌ FAIL:", n_disagree, "cell(s) disagree between the corrplot and the table.\n")
  which(corrplot_sig != table_sig, arr.ind = TRUE) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    mutate(row_label = all_pub_labels[row], col_label = reactivity_labels[col]) |>
    select(row_label, col_label) |>
    print()
}
```

## Matrix vs. Table Agreement: Depression & BFNES

```{r fdr-audit-dep-bfnes-agree}
# Dep and BFNES analyses have no corrplot — only the FDR tables.
# Check that p_fdr values in the stored objects match a fresh recomputation.

check_fdr <- function(long_df, group_var = "group", raw_col = "p_raw", fdr_col = "p_fdr", label = "") {
  recomputed <- long_df |>
    group_by(.data[[group_var]]) |>
    mutate(p_fdr_check = round(p.adjust(.data[[raw_col]], method = "fdr"), 4)) |>
    ungroup()

  n_mismatch <- sum(
    abs(recomputed[[fdr_col]] - recomputed$p_fdr_check) > 1e-6,
    na.rm = TRUE
  )

  if (n_mismatch == 0) {
    cat("✅ PASS", label, "— stored p_fdr matches recomputed FDR on all rows.\n")
  } else {
    cat("❌ FAIL", label, "—", n_mismatch, "row(s) differ.\n")
  }
}

check_fdr(dep_corr_long,   label = "CES-DC × biomarker levels")
check_fdr(bfnes_corr_long, label = "BFNES × biomarker levels")

# Reactivity tables use domain grouping
check_fdr(dep_react_corrs,   group_var = "domain", label = "CES-DC × reactivity")
check_fdr(bfnes_react_corrs, group_var = "domain", label = "BFNES × reactivity")
```

# Supplementary: Responder vs. Non-responder Analyses

*This section is exploratory and supplementary — it was not part of the three pre-registered hypotheses. Dichotomizing a continuous reactivity measure into "responder"/"non-responder" throws away information and loses statistical power relative to treating reactivity as continuous (as the main analyses do). The "any post-baseline increase" threshold used below is also lenient: a single noisy sample above baseline is enough to be classified a responder, so measurement noise alone can inflate the responder group. Finally, the four steps below (responder definition, trajectory plots, the primary CES-DC test, and the exploratory extension) are not multiplicity-controlled against each other — only the 7 biomarker tests within each step are FDR-corrected. Treat this section as hypothesis-generating, not confirmatory.*

## Responder Definition & Counts

For each biomarker, participants are classified using a lenient "any post-baseline increase" rule: **Responder** = at least one of T2, T3, or T4 exceeds T1 (`max(T2, T3, T4) > T1`); **Non-responder** = no post-baseline sample exceeds T1. Participants need at least one non-missing post-T1 sample to be classified; otherwise they are excluded as insufficient data.

This differs from the peak-based reactivity measure used in the main analysis (Hypothesis 1a continued) in two ways: it also considers T2 (the primary analysis only compares T1 to the larger of T3/T4), and it only requires *any single* post-baseline sample to exceed baseline rather than requiring the *larger of two* samples to exceed baseline. As a result, this responder definition is more lenient and is expected to classify more participants as "responders" than would show significant peak reactivity by the primary criterion.

```{r resp-define, echo=FALSE}
classify_responder <- function(data, value_col) {
  data |>
    select(SampleID, Time, value = all_of(value_col)) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = Time, values_from = value, names_prefix = "T", values_fn = mean) |>
    rowwise() |>
    mutate(
      post_max = suppressWarnings(max(c_across(any_of(c("T2", "T3", "T4"))), na.rm = TRUE)),
      post_max = if_else(is.infinite(post_max), NA_real_, post_max),
      responder_status = case_when(
        is.na(T1) | is.na(post_max) ~ NA_character_,
        post_max > T1                ~ "Responder",
        TRUE                          ~ "Non-responder"
      )
    ) |>
    ungroup() |>
    select(SampleID, responder_status)
}

responder_specs <- list(
  "CRP"          = list(data = sos_crp_panel,       col = "CRP_log"),
  "IL-10"        = list(data = sos_cytokines_panel, col = "IL10_log"),
  "IL-6"         = list(data = sos_cytokines_panel, col = "IL6_log"),
  "TNF-alpha"    = list(data = sos_cytokines_panel, col = "TNFalpha_log"),
  "DHEA"         = list(data = sos_hormones_panel,  col = "DHEA_log"),
  "Testosterone" = list(data = sos_hormones_panel,  col = "Testosterone_log"),
  "Cortisol"     = list(data = sos_hormones_panel,  col = "Cortisol_log")
)

biomarker_levels <- c("CRP", "IL-10", "IL-6", "TNF-α", "DHEA", "Testosterone", "Cortisol")

responder_df <- imap_dfr(responder_specs, function(spec, nm) {
  classify_responder(spec$data, spec$col) |> mutate(biomarker = nm)
}) |>
  mutate(
    biomarker = recode(biomarker, "TNF-alpha" = "TNF-α"),
    biomarker = factor(biomarker, levels = biomarker_levels)
  )

responder_summary <- responder_df |>
  group_by(biomarker) |>
  summarise(
    n_responder    = sum(responder_status == "Responder", na.rm = TRUE),
    n_nonresponder = sum(responder_status == "Non-responder", na.rm = TRUE),
    n_excluded     = sum(is.na(responder_status)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    n_classified  = n_responder + n_nonresponder,
    pct_responder = round(100 * n_responder / n_classified, 1)
  )

print(responder_summary, n = 20)

responder_summary |>
  select(biomarker, n_responder, pct_responder, n_nonresponder, n_excluded) |>
  kable(col.names = c("Biomarker", "n Responders", "% Responders", "n Non-responders", "n Excluded"),
        caption = "Responder classification counts by biomarker (any post-baseline sample > T1)") |>
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = "hover", full_width = FALSE)
```

```{r resp-vs-peak, echo=FALSE}
peak_positive <- bind_rows(
  sos_crp_wide       |> transmute(SampleID, biomarker = "CRP",          peak_reactive = crp_peak  > CRP_log_1),
  sos_cytokines_wide |> transmute(SampleID, biomarker = "IL-10",        peak_reactive = il10_peak > IL10_log_1),
  sos_cytokines_wide |> transmute(SampleID, biomarker = "IL-6",         peak_reactive = il6_peak  > IL6_log_1),
  sos_cytokines_wide |> transmute(SampleID, biomarker = "TNF-α",   peak_reactive = tnfa_peak > TNFalpha_log_1),
  sos_hormones_wide  |> transmute(SampleID, biomarker = "DHEA",         peak_reactive = dhea_peak > DHEA_log_1),
  sos_hormones_wide  |> transmute(SampleID, biomarker = "Testosterone", peak_reactive = test_peak > Testosterone_log_1),
  sos_hormones_wide  |> transmute(SampleID, biomarker = "Cortisol",     peak_reactive = cort_peak > Cortisol_log_1)
) |>
  mutate(biomarker = factor(biomarker, levels = biomarker_levels))

resp_vs_peak <- responder_df |>
  filter(!is.na(responder_status)) |>
  inner_join(peak_positive, by = c("SampleID", "biomarker")) |>
  filter(!is.na(peak_reactive)) |>
  group_by(biomarker) |>
  summarise(
    n                       = n(),
    n_responder             = sum(responder_status == "Responder"),
    n_responder_also_peak   = sum(responder_status == "Responder" & peak_reactive),
    pct_responder_also_peak = round(100 * n_responder_also_peak / n_responder, 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(resp_vs_peak, n = 20)

resp_vs_peak |>
  kable(col.names = c("Biomarker", "n (both defined)", "n Responders (any-increase)",
                       "...also peak-reactive (T3/T4 > T1)", "% overlap"),
        caption = "How the lenient any-increase responder definition compares to the peak-based (T3/T4 max) reactivity criterion") |>
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = "hover", full_width = FALSE)
```

```{r resp-counts-results-vals, echo=FALSE, include=FALSE}

resp_overlap_range <- paste0(min(resp_vs_peak$pct_responder_also_peak), "%–", max(resp_vs_peak$pct_responder_also_peak), "%")
```

**Results.** The proportion classified as responders under this lenient "any post-baseline increase" rule ranged from `r resp_pct_range` across the 7 biomarkers. Only `r resp_overlap_range` of responders (by this definition) also met the stricter peak-based reactivity criterion (T3/T4 max exceeding T1) used in the main analysis, confirming that the two definitions capture meaningfully different — and only partially overlapping — groups; the any-increase rule is substantially more permissive.

## Trajectory Plots

Each panel shows the mean (± SE) log-transformed trajectory across T1–T4 for responders vs. non-responders, with faint individual-participant lines in the background.

```{r resp-trajectory-data, echo=FALSE}
traj_data <- imap_dfr(responder_specs, function(spec, nm) {
  rs <- classify_responder(spec$data, spec$col)
  spec$data |>
    select(SampleID, Time, value = all_of(spec$col)) |>
    filter(!is.na(value)) |>
    left_join(rs, by = "SampleID") |>
    filter(!is.na(responder_status)) |>
    mutate(biomarker = nm)
}) |>
  mutate(
    biomarker = recode(biomarker, "TNF-alpha" = "TNF-α"),
    biomarker = factor(biomarker, levels = biomarker_levels)
  )

traj_summary <- traj_data |>
  group_by(biomarker, Time, responder_status) |>
  summarise(mean_val = mean(value), se_val = sd(value) / sqrt(n()), n = n(), .groups = "drop")
```

```{r resp-trajectory-plot, fig.width=12, fig.height=8}
ggplot(traj_data, aes(x = Time, y = value, group = SampleID, color = responder_status)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.25, alpha = 0.12) +
  geom_line(data = traj_summary,
            aes(x = Time, y = mean_val, group = responder_status, color = responder_status),
            linewidth = 1.3, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  geom_errorbar(data = traj_summary,
                aes(x = Time, y = mean_val, ymin = mean_val - se_val, ymax = mean_val + se_val,
                    group = responder_status, color = responder_status),
                width = 0.15, linewidth = 0.6, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  geom_point(data = traj_summary,
             aes(x = Time, y = mean_val, group = responder_status, color = responder_status),
             size = 1.8, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:4, labels = paste0("T", 1:4)) +
  scale_color_viridis_d(name = NULL, begin = 0.2, end = 0.75) +
  facet_wrap(~biomarker, scales = "free_y", ncol = 4) +
  labs(x = "Timepoint", y = "Concentration (log-transformed)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
        legend.position = "bottom")
```

**Results.** By construction, responder trajectories rise above T1 at some point post-baseline while non-responder trajectories stay flat or decline; the value of this figure is in showing *where* that separation occurs (e.g., whether it appears already at T2, or only at T3/T4) and how much within-group spread (faint lines) surrounds each group mean. -->

<!-- ## Depressive Symptoms (Primary Supplementary Test)

For each biomarker, we tested whether CES-DC total score differs between responders and non-responders (Welch two-sample t-test; Wilcoxon rank-sum reported alongside as a robustness check given the likely skew of self-report symptom totals). Cohen's *d* uses the pooled-SD convention with the standard large-sample normal-approximation 95% CI; FDR correction is applied to the Welch-test p-values across the 7 biomarkers.

```{r resp-group-test-fn, echo=FALSE}
run_group_test <- function(rs_df, outcome_df, outcome_col) {
  d <- rs_df |>
    filter(!is.na(responder_status)) |>
    inner_join(outcome_df, by = "SampleID") |>
    filter(!is.na(.data[[outcome_col]]))

  resp    <- d[[outcome_col]][d$responder_status == "Responder"]
  nonresp <- d[[outcome_col]][d$responder_status == "Non-responder"]

  if (length(resp) < 2 || length(nonresp) < 2) {
    return(tibble(
      n_responder = length(resp), n_nonresponder = length(nonresp),
      mean_responder = NA_real_, sd_responder = NA_real_,
      mean_nonresponder = NA_real_, sd_nonresponder = NA_real_,
      t_stat = NA_real_, df = NA_real_, p_welch = NA_real_,
      W_stat = NA_real_, p_wilcox = NA_real_,
      cohen_d = NA_real_, d_lower = NA_real_, d_upper = NA_real_
    ))
  }

  tt <- t.test(resp, nonresp)  # Welch by default (unequal variances)
  wt <- suppressWarnings(wilcox.test(resp, nonresp))

  n1 <- length(resp); n2 <- length(nonresp)
  pooled_sd <- sqrt(((n1 - 1) * var(resp) + (n2 - 1) * var(nonresp)) / (n1 + n2 - 2))
  d_val <- (mean(resp) - mean(nonresp)) / pooled_sd
  se_d  <- sqrt((n1 + n2) / (n1 * n2) + d_val^2 / (2 * (n1 + n2 - 2)))

  tibble(
    n_responder = n1, n_nonresponder = n2,
    mean_responder = mean(resp), sd_responder = sd(resp),
    mean_nonresponder = mean(nonresp), sd_nonresponder = sd(nonresp),
    t_stat = unname(tt$statistic), df = unname(tt$parameter), p_welch = tt$p.value,
    W_stat = unname(wt$statistic), p_wilcox = wt$p.value,
    cohen_d = d_val, d_lower = d_val - 1.96 * se_d, d_upper = d_val + 1.96 * se_d
  )
}

responder_by_biomarker <- split(responder_df, responder_df$biomarker)
```

```{r resp-cesdc-test, echo=FALSE}
cesdc_results <- imap_dfr(responder_by_biomarker, function(rs_df, nm) {

}) |>
  mutate(p_fdr = p.adjust(p_welch, method = "fdr"))

print(cesdc_results, n = 20)

cesdc_results |>
```
